title: An encyclopedia of human enhancer-gene regulatory interactions.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed both labelled benchmark tables from GitHub tag v1.0.0 (MIT licence, no login): EPCrisprBenchmark_combined_data.training_K562.GRCh38.tsv.gz (996,546 bytes, md5 11aed1393bcee2173297869d3e8dae67, 4.33 MB unzipped, 10,356 rows x 42 columns) and EPCrisprBenchmark_combined_data.heldout_5_cell_types.GRCh38.tsv.gz (373,837 bytes, md5 10749629f0626f25bb0e7b99b57bdabb, 1.78 MB unzipped, 4,378 rows x 42 columns). Verified firsthand: zero missing values in any column of either file; zero duplicate element-gene-cell-type rows; zero exact element-gene overlap between the two files; 471 positives / 9,885 negatives in training and 190 / 4,188 in held-out (label column 'Regulated'); 5,638 unique element coordinate triples and 2,455 unique transcription start sites across both files; 23 chromosomes; one element of zero width; a four-digit publication year parses from the 'Reference' column for 100% of 14,734 rows (2019 n=5,740; 2021 n=3,935; 2025 n=3,173; 2020 n=1,306; 2024 n=396; 2023 n=184). I also computed my own dummy baselines: positive rate 4.55% (training) and 4.34% (held-out); average precision of a distance-only ranker 0.438 (training) and 0.320 (held-out); of DNase signal divided by distance 0.503 and 0.429. I read the column-by-column README in the same GitHub directory, which documents all 42 columns with types and units. I confirmed the Synapse entity syn70814727 (extended-feature version) returns metadata anonymously but refuses download with HTTP 403 'Anonymous users have only READ access permission'.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All performance numbers for ENCODE-rE2G and its competitors (area under the precision-recall curve 0.66 for the DNase-only model and 0.74 for the Extended model; precision at 70% recall 58% and 73%; the Activity-by-Contact comparison values 0.56 and 0.61; held-out precision 53.2%), the hold-one-chromosome-out cross-validation design, the 92,176,227 predicted interactions across 1,458 biosamples, the count of 616 competing models benchmarked, and the statement that held-out positives lacking H3K27ac signal were deliberately removed. I did not download the ENCODE portal prediction files, the Hi-C data, the GTEx expression quantitative trait locus files, or the Synapse baseline-prediction bundle (syn58896208).

a1_downloadable.note: Both labelled tables download anonymously from a GitHub release tag under an MIT licence; I fetched and parsed them. Caveat: the richer feature version on Synapse (syn70814727) refused anonymous download with HTTP 403, so that variant needs a free account.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Verified in the files: 'Regulated' is a ready-made boolean column (661 True across both files) and 'EffectSize' is a ready-made signed continuous column. Nothing has to be joined or constructed.

a3_inputs_present.note: Measured chromatin inputs sit in the same rows (H3K27ac, DNase, CTCF, H3K27me3, H3K4me1 signal plus distance to the gene's start). DNA sequence is not in the file but GRCh38 coordinates are, so sequence is one reference-genome lookup away for 5,638 elements.

a4_units_stated.note: The directory README gives type and unit for all 42 columns: signal in RPM (reads per million), distance in base pairs, power and probability columns bounded 0-1, effect size as a signed fraction of expression. Verified by reading it.

a5_enough_rows.note: Counted firsthand: 10,356 training + 4,378 held-out rows, 661 positives total. Above the 1,500-row bar, though the scarce class (661 positives) is the real sample size.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 6.1 MB of tab-separated text; ~15 MB more if element and promoter sequences are fetched per region
a6_fits_laptop.note: Both files unzip to 6.1 MB combined. No GPU needed for the tabular baseline; frozen DNA-model embeddings for ~8,000 short sequences run on CPU.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Exact match: paper says 10,356 tested pairs with 471 positives and 4,378 held-out pairs with 190 positives; the files give precisely those numbers, as does the README. One cosmetic discrepancy: the paper's text and one extended-data caption say 4,405 held-out pairs before a filter, while the distributed file has 4,378.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels trace to physical measurement: CRISPR interference silencing of an element followed by measured expression of the nearby gene (flow-cytometry RNA readout, single-cell RNA sequencing, or targeted amplicon sequencing). 'Regulated' is a documented threshold on that measurement (adjusted p < 0.05 and negative effect). One real caveat I verified: in the held-out file all 190 positives fall in the two H3K27ac categories and zero fall among the 1,438 CTCF / H3K27me3 / no-H3K27ac elements, because the authors removed H3K27ac-negative positives. H3K27ac is therefore partly determined by the label in that file, which flatters any model using it. The 'direct_vs_indirect_negative' column is a model-estimated probability, not a measurement, so it must not be used as a feature.

B1.why: Two files, identical 42-column schema, one row per element-gene-cell-type; no join needed. Verified in files.

B2.why: Gzipped tab-separated; pandas read both on first try, no type coercion warnings. Verified.

B3.why: Binary label harmonised by authors, but effect sizes come from three assay families with differing power. Paper text.

B4.why: Zero missing values in all 42 columns of both files; no censored or qualitative entries. Verified.

B5.why: Zero duplicate element-gene-cell-type rows; zero overlap between training and held-out files. Verified.

B6.why: README in the same directory documents every one of 42 columns with type and unit. Read it.

C1.why: Framed as how far sequence-plus-distance gets without cell-type assays, the answer is informative either way.

C2.why: This file is the field's reference benchmark; ENCODE-rE2G, Activity-by-Contact, GraphReg, EPIraction, AlphaGenome all open and honestly evaluated on it.

C3.why: Only angle left is an honest-re-evaluation audit plus small-backbone transfer; AlphaGenome already covered sequence-only on this exact data.

C4.why: Ground truth requires genome-scale CRISPR interference screens costing months of lab work per cell type. Paper methods.

C5.why: Published 0.66 and 0.74 area under precision-recall curve, plus my own measured distance-only baseline of 0.438.

D1.why: GRCh38 coordinates let open-weight DNA models (HyenaDNA, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer) read element and promoter sequence.

D2.why: Only 5,638 unique elements and 2,455 promoters; embeddings cache once on CPU, head is a logistic regression.

D3.why: Data MIT-licensed (verified via GitHub application programming interface); HyenaDNA is Apache-2.0, DNABERT-2 permissive.

E1.why: Hold-one-chromosome-out (23 chromosomes present), held-out cell type, held-out assay, and a parseable publication year. Verified.

E2.why: 23 chromosomes, 5 cell types, 11 source datasets, 6 publication years; all counted in the files.

E3.why: I computed them: 4.55% positive rate, distance-only average precision 0.438, DNase-over-distance 0.503.

E4.why: Five PowerAtEffectSize columns quantify detection limits per pair; overlapping source screens allow disagreement estimates. Verified columns exist.

E5.why: Model must recover the distance decay and the H3K27ac/DNase enrichment, and the textbook MYC and GATA1 K562 enhancers are present.

E6.why: Label shuffling and feature-block ablation are trivial on a 6 MB table; the paper itself ran leave-one-feature-out.

E7.why: Separate held-out file of 4,378 pairs in 4 new cell types and 3 new assays, plus a 100%-parseable year for a temporal split. Verified.

E8.why: ENCODE-rE2G code is MIT-licensed with a Snakemake pipeline and published numbers; note the baseline bundle on Synapse needs a free account.

G1.why: Ensembl gene identifiers, gene symbols and GRCh38 coordinates all present as columns. Verified in files.

G2.why: GTEx and Human Protein Atlas join on Ensembl gene; ENCODE candidate cis-regulatory element catalogue joins on coordinates.

G3.why: Gene-level joins are one-to-one on 2,343 Ensembl identifiers; coordinate joins need a documented overlap rule.

G4.why: Asks whether gene-level expression breadth explains where chromatin-based enhancer-gene models fail; neither resource answers that alone.

H1.why: 9,885 training and 4,188 held-out negatives, each power-filtered so absence of effect is meaningful. Verified counts.

H2.why: Training set is K562 only (verified); held-out adds 4 cell types but with just 15, 16 and 7 positives in three of them.

H3.why: Claim statable in one sentence: ranking only among pairs the screens had power to test, mostly in K562.

H4.why: Paper names four failure modes explicitly (indirect effects, weak enhancers, no-H3K27ac elements, ubiquitous genes). Paper text.

I1.why: Engreitz lab at Stanford, the ENCODE consortium and variant-to-gene mapping groups maintain and use this benchmark.

I2.why: Would only redirect assay-collection choices if the result were strong; the paper already runs its own assay-utility analysis.

I3.why: Precision at 70% recall is literally the threshold the authors used to call their 92 million interactions. Paper text.

I4.why: I measured distance alone at 0.438 average precision versus a 0.045 base rate; simple features do much of the work.

J1.why: Grouped splits, class imbalance, transfer across cell types, frozen-backbone embeddings: all the techniques worth learning.

J2.why: Regulatory genomics is checkable against textbook loci, and the owning lab is at the evaluator's own institution.

J3.why: The leakage audit I already found (held-out positives all H3K27ac-positive by construction) is shareable even if no model works.

J4.why: No time budget set yet; the work plausibly fits two weekends but that has not been committed.

J5.why: No kill date or condition written down anywhere in the repository notes.

existing_models.name: ENCODE-rE2G (logistic regression on chromatin and 3D-contact features, this paper)
existing_models.score_and_split: Area under the precision-recall curve 0.66 (DNase-only) and 0.74 (Extended), precision at 70% recall 58% and 73%, under hold-one-chromosome-out cross-validation on the same 10,356-pair file I downloaded; 53.2% precision on the 4,378-pair held-out file
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: All models, theirs included, fail on pairs driven by indirect (trans) effects, on weak enhancers with small effect sizes, on elements lacking H3K27ac, and on ubiquitously expressed genes (1.5% versus 7.6% positive rate); they also failed to predict three well-characterised MYC enhancers ~2 Mb away

existing_models.name: ABC / Activity-by-Contact (enhancer activity times 3D contact frequency)
existing_models.score_and_split: Area under the precision-recall curve 0.56 (DNase plus average Hi-C) and 0.61 (DNase times H3K27ac plus cell-type Hi-C) on the same 10,356-pair benchmark
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Assumes enhancers act additively and independently, which this paper's enhancer-synergy analysis contradicts

existing_models.name: Enformer (sequence-to-function transformer, Google DeepMind)
existing_models.score_and_split: Benchmarked by this paper among 616 models on the same 10,356-pair file and reported to perform worse than ENCODE-rE2G; exact value in their Supplementary Table 3, which I did not open
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Systematically underpredicts the magnitude of distal element knockdown effects, with the gap widening with distance

existing_models.name: AlphaGenome (sequence-to-function model, Google DeepMind, Nature 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported by its own authors as zero-shot enhancer-gene linking area under the precision-recall curve on this very ENCODE-rE2G CRISPR interference dataset, stratified by element-to-start-site distance; I read this in secondary sources, not in the AlphaGenome paper itself
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Still underestimates distal enhancer effect magnitude

backbone.name: HyenaDNA-small (open DNA sequence model, Apache-2.0) or DNABERT-2, reading the ~500 bp element and a 2 kb window around the gene's transcription start site
backbone.hardware: 16 GB laptop CPU; ~8,100 sequences to embed once and cache
backbone.licence: Data MIT (verified); HyenaDNA Apache-2.0; AlphaGenome weights non-commercial if used as an optional comparison

integration.partner_dataset: GTEx v10 median expression per tissue (joined to get each gene's expression breadth) plus the ENCODE candidate cis-regulatory element catalogue
integration.join_key: measuredGeneEnsemblId (2,343 unique Ensembl gene identifiers, present as a column) for GTEx; GRCh38 chrom/start/end for the element catalogue
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do gene-level properties measured outside this experiment, above all how many tissues a gene is expressed in, explain which enhancer-gene pairs every chromatin-based model gets wrong?

controls.positive_control: Two, chosen in advance: the model must reproduce the distance decay (my distance-only ranker already reaches 0.438 average precision against a 0.045 base rate) and must rank the textbook MYC, GATA1 and HBE1 K562 enhancers, which are in the file, among its top predictions.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the 'Regulated' column within chromosome and confirm average precision collapses to 0.045; ablate the chromatin feature block and the sequence feature block separately; replace sequence embeddings with same-shape random vectors.
controls.external_validation: The separate 4,378-pair held-out file covering 4 new cell types and 3 new assay types, plus a temporal split on the publication year that parses from the 'Reference' column for 100% of rows (train on 2019-2021, test on 2023-2025).

honest_claim_h3: Among distal element-gene pairs that CRISPR interference screens had at least 80% statistical power to test, overwhelmingly in the K562 leukaemia cell line, this model ranks which pairs showed a statistically significant drop in gene expression when the element was silenced; it says nothing about untestable pairs, about elements the screens never targeted, or about cell types outside the five represented.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use an enhancer's own DNA sequence and its distance to a gene to predict whether switching the enhancer off lowers that gene's expression.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example is one regulatory element paired with one nearby gene: the element's GRCh38 coordinates (so its ~500 base pairs of sequence can be read), its distance to the gene's start, and measured chromatin signals at the element. I verified 10,356 such examples in the K562 training table and 4,378 in a separate held-out table across five cell types, 14,734 in total.
plain_idea.predict: A yes/no call on whether silencing that element significantly reduced the gene's expression, and optionally the size of the reduction. The truth comes from CRISPR interference experiments that switch the element off and then measure the gene's messenger RNA by flow cytometry, single-cell sequencing or targeted sequencing; 661 of the 14,734 pairs are positive.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Mapping which enhancer controls which gene currently requires a months-long CRISPR screen per cell type, so anyone interpreting disease-associated variants in non-coding DNA wants a cheap substitute. Even a failure maps precisely how much of enhancer-gene regulation is invisible to DNA sequence alone.

pitch.headline: The field's reference enhancer-gene benchmark, 14,734 CRISPR-measured pairs in 6 MB, zero missing values, MIT licence, one download.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: I opened both files and found 42 fully documented columns, 0 missing values, 0 duplicate rows, 0 leakage between the training and held-out splits, row and positive counts exactly matching the paper (10,356/471 and 4,378/190), and a publication year parseable for 100% of rows so a temporal split costs one line of code.
pitch.the_win: Beat my measured distance-only baseline of 0.438 average precision using DNA sequence and distance alone, with no cell-type chromatin measurement, and close some of the gap to the paper's published 0.66 (DNase-based ENCODE-rE2G) on the same hold-one-chromosome-out split.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: Two findings already in hand are shareable regardless: all 190 held-out positives sit in the two H3K27ac-positive categories while 1,438 H3K27ac-negative elements are all negatives, so the held-out split flatters any model using H3K27ac; and the held-out set has only 15 positives in WTC11, 16 in GM12878 and 7 in Jurkat, so its cross-cell-type claim rests on K562 and HCT116.
pitch.who_wants_it: The Engreitz lab at Stanford, who own this benchmark and the MIT-licensed benchmarking pipeline, and ENCODE variant-to-gene groups deciding whether to pay for DNase sequencing in a new cell type or lean on sequence models.

ml_idea: Binary classification of 'Regulated' with grouped evaluation. Features in three blocks: (1) sequence, from frozen HyenaDNA or DNABERT-2 embeddings of the ~500 bp element and a 2 kb promoter window, cached once for 5,638 elements and 2,455 transcription start sites; (2) geometry, distance to the start site alone; (3) chromatin, the measured H3K27ac/DNase/CTCF signals already in the table. Evaluate with hold-one-chromosome-out cross-validation on the K562 training file, matching the paper's split so its 0.66 and 0.74 numbers are directly comparable, then transfer to the 4,378-pair held-out file broken out per cell type and per assay, and separately under a temporal split on publication year. The headline experiment is block ablation: how much of the chromatin-based model's performance is recoverable from sequence plus distance, which needs no new experiment in a new cell type. Stratify all errors by the four weaknesses the authors named (indirect effects, small effect size, no H3K27ac, ubiquitously expressed genes) and, via a GTEx join on Ensembl gene, test whether expression breadth predicts the residual error.

effort.compute_note: Tables are 6.1 MB unzipped and I timed their parse at under a second, so the chromatin-only feature table is ready in minutes. The 3-hour figure is for adding sequence: ~8,100 regions fetched per-coordinate from the UCSC API (~15 MB, keeping the working set tiny) or by downloading GRCh38 once and discarding it. Embedding time is an estimate, not timed: ~8,100 sequences at roughly 1 per second on a laptop CPU with a small DNA model. Cross-validation time is an estimate for 23-fold logistic regression or gradient boosting on 10,356 rows by ~60 features.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count positives per held-out cell type before anything else. I did it: WTC11 15, GM12878 16, Jurkat 7, HCT116 34, K562 118. Three of the five cell types cannot support a per-cell-type performance estimate, so any 'generalises across five cell types' claim has to be scaled back to two.

verdict_reason: The data is as close to perfect as this checklist ever sees: Part A passes on every item verified in the files (14,734 rows, 661 positives, 0 missing, 0 duplicates, 0 train/test leakage, counts matching the paper exactly, every column documented, MIT licence, 6 MB), and Part B scores 11/12. It is parked, not recommended, on C2 alone. This file is the field's standard benchmark: ENCODE-rE2G, Activity-by-Contact, GraphReg, EPIraction, EpiMap, Enformer, scE2G and AlphaGenome have all been evaluated on it, with open code and honest splits (hold-one-chromosome-out plus a held-out cell-type set), which is exactly the crowded-plus-reproducible-plus-honestly-evaluated combination the checklist calls fatal. AlphaGenome's authors have already published zero-shot results on this exact dataset, so even the sequence-only angle is taken. Worth keeping on the shelf as an evaluation target for any future enhancer model, and worth revisiting if the two real audit findings here (held-out positives are H3K27ac-positive by construction; three of five held-out cell types have fewer than 20 positives) turn out to be unreported.
